Understand LFP growth in global energy storage and Korea's ESS central contract market.
ESS stores electricity for later use

An Energy Storage System (ESS) includes batteries, a power conversion system (PCS), controls, cooling and fire protection. It smooths renewable output and shifts electricity supply to periods of higher demand.
MW measures instantaneous power; MWh measures stored energy
. A 100 MW / 600 MWh system provides roughly six hours of rated output under rated conditions.
In new battery storage installations worldwide,
are currently the most common. The IEA reports about 80% of new storage in 2023 and over 90% of new stationary battery installations in 2025. These figures refer to
, not the share of all installed ESS capacity in Korea.
Which batteries are gaining ground, and why?
Lead-acid is inexpensive with established supply and recycling, but is heavy and has limitations in usable energy and cycle life. Lithium-ion offers advantages in efficiency and installation space.
Lead-acid has not disappeared. It remains in UPS and backup-power applications.
High energy per unit mass and volume, supported by mature Korean supply technology. Useful where installation space is limited.
Thermal management, raw-material prices and operating conditions matter. Korean and global markets evolve at different speeds.

LFP contains no nickel or cobalt and offers long cycle life and relatively high thermal stability. Stationary ESS faces fewer weight constraints than vehicles, so lifetime cost often matters more than energy density.
Lower energy density, cold-weather performance and state-of-charge estimation remain challenges. LFP can still catch fire, so system safety design is essential.
Exploring sodium-ion, flow batteries and more
Material options and long-duration storage needs drive interest. Flow batteries allow tank capacity and system power to be sized relatively independently.
These technologies have not replaced the global ESS mainstream. Cost, efficiency, footprint and supply scale still need validation.

This does not mean every ESS has switched from NCM to LFP. LFP is increasingly selected for new investments. Samsung SDI presents NCA in SBB 1.7 and LFP in SBB 2.0; LG Energy Solution also offers NCM(A) and LFP.

What is Korea's ESS central contract market?

Korea Power Exchange announces required locations and capacity. Developers bid a price and a plan to build and operate ESS. Selected projects provide storage and delivery capability under a contract and receive settlement payments.
This is separate from battery product procurement and hydrogen-generation HPS/CHPS tenders
Price, site, equipment and safety plan
The September 22, 2026 notice seeks mainland capacity of

, each sized for six hours of storage. Target completion is February 2029. The mainland notice specifies a 15-year term with 50 points for price and 50 for non-price factors, including safety, technical performance, grid and industrial contributions. Tender capacity is not awarded capacity.
Choosing LFP does not automatically win a contract.
Evaluation covers fire prevention and response, certification, efficiency, life and grid conditions, as well as chemistry. The notice does not permit mixing NCM and LFP within one bid configuration.

The tender price unit, KRW/kW-h, is a contract and settlement unit tied to available power and time. It must not be directly compared with battery purchase prices in KRW/kWh. Rare earths and critical minerals are different

Lithium, nickel, cobalt and platinum are not rare-earth elements. Some NiMH hydrogen-storage alloys contain rare earths such as lanthanum. USGS estimates 2025 lithium mine output at about 290,000 tonnes excluding the United States, but this cannot be converted directly into a maximum annual battery output. Refining, recycling, allocation between uses and material input per product all differ.

Are fuel cells storage devices or generators?

Fuel cells directly convert the chemical energy of a fuel and oxidant into electricity through electrochemical reactions. They generate while fuel and air are supplied, unlike secondary batteries that recharge their internal reactants.
Electrons and ions follow different paths
The basic reaction using hydrogen directly is
. Systems that reform natural gas into hydrogen, or use carbon-containing fuels, can also emit CO₂.
Names such as PEMFC and SOFC refer to the electrolyte

Fuel cells are classified mainly by electrolyte type, which determines the mobile ion, operating temperature and fuel options. DMFC emphasizes the direct use of methanol, rather than a particular electrolyte class.
Polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cell · PEMFC
Relatively low operating temperature and responsive output. Vehicles, mobile and distributed power.
High-temperature operation with fuel flexibility and useful heat. Stationary generation.
Stationary combined heat and power. Heat recovery and system operation are important.
High-temperature operation for large stationary generation and heat use.

Convenient liquid fuel. Portable and remote power; the reaction produces CO₂.
Are hydrogen and clean-hydrogen fuel cells separate technology classes?

A hydrogen fuel cell uses hydrogen as fuel. Clean hydrogen is a certification concept based on greenhouse-gas emissions from hydrogen production and related stages. A clean-hydrogen fuel cell is not a separate electrolyte class; it is a fuel cell using certified clean hydrogen.
Separate device emissions from fuel emissions.

A direct-hydrogen fuel cell produces water, but fossil-based hydrogen production means lifecycle greenhouse-gas emissions are not necessarily zero. Certification and its accounting boundary matter more than hydrogen color labels.
Korea's clean-hydrogen threshold is greenhouse-gas emissions per kilogram of hydrogen of
. CO₂e converts different greenhouse gases to a common carbon-dioxide equivalent. Check the applicable notice and certification criteria for boundaries, grades and transport-related provisions.

Which costs matter for generation projects?

Assess equipment cost (KRW/kW), fuel, efficiency, utilization, stack replacement and maintenance, heat sales and electricity sales terms together. Storage-capacity cost (KRW/kWh) and generating-capacity cost (KRW/kW) are different metrics.

For each project, combine tender revenue with fuel, maintenance and financing costs to calculate generation cost and cash flow. These are business evaluation criteria, not a claim that fuel cells are always cheaper than thermal generation.

Use once, then replace. Useful where storage life and convenience matter more than recharging.

A primary battery converts the chemical energy of stored reactants into electricity. Typical products are not designed for recharging and are unsuitable for repeatedly reversing the used reactants electrically.
Electrons pass through the external circuit
Replace the cell when reactants are depleted
The electrolyte carries ions; electrons flow through the external circuit connected to the device. Electrode–electrolyte combinations determine voltage, current capability, shelf life and cost.
Zinc and manganese dioxide with a chloride-based electrolyte. Low cost, but less suitable for sustained high currents.
Zinc–manganese dioxide electrodes with an alkaline electrolyte. Usually better usable capacity and current capability than zinc–carbon cells.
Metallic lithium anodes. Cathodes distinguish lithium–manganese dioxide, lithium–thionyl chloride and other types. High energy density and long shelf life.
Silver oxide cathodes and zinc anodes. Compact with relatively stable voltage; affected by silver prices.
Zinc reacts with oxygen from the air. Opening the air holes activates the battery; after activation, life decreases even without use.
Chemistry names and sizes are separate classifications

Alkaline describes the electrolyte, silver oxide names the cathode material, and primary lithium usually refers to the metallic lithium anode. Primary battery names therefore do not follow a single classification rule.
AA, AAA and coin refer to size and shape.

AA products include alkaline primary and nickel-metal hydride secondary batteries with different voltages and operating requirements. Primary lithium and lithium-ion secondary batteries must also be distinguished.

First check the required voltage and size, then compare current demand, temperature range, storage period and replacement interval. For frequent use, consider rechargeable lifetime costs. Do not recharge ordinary primary cells; collect used batteries separately for recycling.

Batteries that reverse chemical reactions through charging for repeated use. Different names use different classification criteria.

During discharge, electrode reactions send electrons through the external circuit to supply power. During charging, an external source drives the reaction in reverse to store energy again. Ions move through the electrolyte to maintain charge balance.
Rechargeable does not mean unlimited life. Electrode and electrolyte side reactions, structural changes, temperature and operating conditions reduce capacity and power over time.
Are all secondary batteries named after the cathode?
LFP, NMC (NCM), NCA, LCO and LMO name the cathode active material of lithium-ion batteries.

This rule does not apply to every secondary battery. Cathode materials form the positive electrode, and these abbreviations specifically identify the active material participating in energy-storage reactions.
